details:
Each world needs VRCWorld object. That is clear enough.
The looking direction of VRCWorld is done at blue arrow (you need set it Local), because you will spawn there with this looking direction.
For uploading world picture, the camera is generated named VRCCam.
But for weird reason, the VRCCam is positioned with opposite direction. It means the camera will look 180 degrees away, and not in the same looking direction of VRCWorld.
This wrong rotation problem exists since 2018, and it's never simply fixed in SDKs. Today, it's still wrong set.
Because if you upload the world, camera should not look other way. It doesn't match where it should look. The creator must correct it every time again to look in correct direction.
Also, the camera position is wrong, its at 0 height. It will go inside the "floor" where VRCWorld is placed. This is also incorrect set.
The VRCCam must set at around 1,8 metres height, the common avatar looking height. And it must look in same direction as VRCWorld object.
Because this problem is not really a bug, it's never adjusted for years. But it's lazy and not great setup by putting at 0 height and looking 180 degrees off. Who made this setup? We know all this is just not right default look.
Some new creators even upload it without changing VRCCam, makes the world will look wrong (like looking to wall or half in floor). And every time adjust it again is just not great.
The solution is very easy. But i think no one developer care about it because it's not a bug. But it's "dirtyness" of setup, not proper setup.
title: VRCCam vs VRCWorld problem looking direction
